FIB_PLUS	<p>8341_7c21</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d10;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6e5d10;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d10;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #246298;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #246298;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246298;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e3878;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8e3878;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e3878;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cpx, +++, cpx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and whole number. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f540c;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7f540c;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f540c;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e3878;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8e3878;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e3878;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cnt, +++, cnt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>d814_d256</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #206d4c;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #206d4c;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #206d4c;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3755bb;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3755bb;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f540c;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7f540c;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f540c;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7c4096;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7c4096;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f540c;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7f540c;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f540c;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #246298;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #246298;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246298;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e3878;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8e3878;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e3878;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dkx, +++, dkx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>c777_b94a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f470f;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8f470f;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f470f;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #206d4c;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #206d4c;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #206d4c;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7c4096;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7c4096;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>06dc_b5a1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d10;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6e5d10;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d10;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6344b9;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6344b9;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>bd99_7334</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #366d27;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #366d27;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #366d27;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #246298;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #246298;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246298;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e3878;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8e3878;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>2ffd_d3ea</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f470f;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8f470f;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f470f;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #366d27;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #366d27;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #366d27;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #246298;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #246298;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and whole number. Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". FIB_PLUS	<p>e685_585a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #5a6500;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #246298;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #246298;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246298;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983653;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #983653;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983653;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dhj, +++, dhj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8f470f;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8f470f;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096c62;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6344b9;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6344b9;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. whole number. map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and pick a new pair of genes until all pairs are Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units".
